scope: Independent read-only spec compliance, then code-quality review of frozen proxy and service ownership fixes. No production edits, builds, application/QQ runtime, profiles or cache access.

specCompliance.provider: Main recovery scope conforms: one transient retry only for unpublished future blocks, retained permits, monotonic remaining retry budget, unchanged initial stream, independent session/identity validation, terminal auth/identity/range/EOF/cancel failures. One malformed Retry-After parsing exception found below.
specCompliance.core: Conforms: existing caller timeout retained, settled slow request retains native ownership/capacity, one bounded completion grace, late replies only release ownership, cleanup across exit/destroy, child/generation fences prevent stale timer killing replacement.

notes: Timer ownership remains in the existing pending map rather than a second parallel request owner.
Recovery does not retry already-published ciphertext or silently replay PCM bytes.
Three sibling future blocks can each recover once; this remains inside the existing global permit bound.
No claim that these synthetic fixes prove the historical real-world playback timeout cause.

findings.title: Reject malformed Retry-After before Date.parse
findings.detail: retryDelay passes every non-digit value into permissive Date.parse. Values '-1' and '1.5' are interpreted as historical dates, producing zero delay and a successful second attempt. The frozen receipt promises malformed Retry-After is terminal. Validate a supported HTTP-date form before parsing, and preserve the current remainder/attempt limits.
findings.impactBoundary: Finite one-retry policy and permit/auth bounds remain intact; this is malformed server-delay handling, not authorization bypass or an infinite retry.
findings.closure: Followup source uses strict IMF-fixdate shape, date-component roundtrip and weekday validation. Independent v2 probe confirms -1 and 1.5 now terminate after one attempt while integer zero still recovers.

cases: Two detached slow requests keep independent grace ownership when one completes; polling cannot renew the remaining grace.
Completing all detached requests releases capacity, clears all recovery timers and cannot overwrite a newer playback cache.
